member.summary: Starts a looping ambience, somewhere in the room.
member.param: The sound, or null to stop whatever is playing.
Where it is, or null to play it at the listener's head.
member.returns: True when something is playing.
member.remarks: A soundtrack says where its sound is and how far it carries — RC1's fountain is at (3113, 114, −2337) and reaches 1,200 units. Played at the head instead, it is as loud across the square as it is standing in it.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.AmbienceAt
member.summary: Where the ambience is in the room, or null when it plays at the head.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.StartAmbience(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GK3Reborn.Formats.Audio.SoundtrackFile})
member.summary: Starts the room's ambience from the soundtracks the scene names.
member.param: What the scene listed.
member.returns: What is playing, or null when none of it could be.

remarks.para: A soundtrack is a little program — pick one of these at random, wait between four and nine seconds, repeat twice — and running it properly is a scheduler of its own. This takes the first sound of the first ambient track and loops it, which gives a room its tone but not its variety.
Deliberately the simple half. The difference is audible over minutes rather than seconds, and a room that hums is much closer to right than a room that is silent.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Sound(GK3Reborn.Game.SoundtrackProgram,GK3Reborn.Formats.Audio.SoundtrackSound)
member.summary: Starts one sound of a soundtrack, and says how long it lasts.
member.param: The soundtrack it belongs to.
The sound, as the file describes it.
member.returns: Its length in seconds, or zero when it could not be played.

remarks.para: A sound that loops is the room's bed: it is what the room sounds like for as long as the player is in it, and it is what the crossfade into the next room fades out. It goes through the same decode-off-the-thread path as before, because a bed is often a five-minute MP3 and decoding one where the room appears is a quarter of a second of nothing happening.

Everything else is a moment — a creak, a bell, a car going past — and is played outright. Those are short, already decoded by the time a room has been in for a minute, and waiting a frame for one would put it after the step that follows it.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Bus(GK3Reborn.Formats.Audio.SoundtrackKind)
member.summary: Which bus a soundtrack's sounds are mixed on.
member.remarks: The file says: SoundType=Music, Ambient or SFX, which is which of the player's own volume sliders it obeys.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.PlacementOf(GK3Reborn.Formats.Audio.SoundtrackSound)
member.summary: Where a soundtrack's sound is, if it says.
member.param: The sound, as its soundtrack describes it.
member.returns: Its placement, or null when it belongs at the listener.

remarks.para: A .STK either gives a sound a place in the room or does not. Those that do carry 3D=1 with a position and a pair of distances — CSE's fountain is 85 to 1,000 units, a passing car is 250 to 2,500 — and those that do not are room tone, which belongs at the head because it comes from everywhere.

A sound that follows something is not placed here. Follow=blk_sedan means the emitter moves with a model, and where that model is at any moment is the room's business rather than this file's; until something asks the room, following sounds play at their authored spot, which is where the model starts.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Listen(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3)
member.summary: Puts the listener where the player is looking from.
member.param: The camera's position.
Which way it looks.
Which way is up for it.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Speak(System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: Says a run of lines, one after another.
member.param: The licence plate the script gave.
How many lines, itself included.
member.returns: How many of them were found.
member.remarks: Anything already being said is abandoned. That is what the original does — a script that starts a conversation while one is running means to replace it — and it is also the only behaviour that cannot deadlock.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Continue(System.Int32)
member.summary: Says the next lines of whatever was last started.
member.param: How many more to say.
member.returns: How many of them were found.

remarks.para: A conversation is written as one plate and then a series of continuations: the script says StartDialogue("1E4CU4OCZ1", 1) and later ContinueDialogue(2), which means the next two in the same sequence. The plate is not repeated, so somebody has to remember where the run had got to.
Continuing when nothing was started says nothing, which is what a script calling it out of order deserves — and is better than guessing at a plate.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Talking
member.summary: Whether anybody is speaking at this moment.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.SecondsOfNext(System.Int32)
member.summary: How long the next lines of the run in progress take.
member.param: How many more.
member.returns: Seconds, or nought when nothing has been started.
member.remarks: What a waited ContinueDialogue is worth. The run's licence plate was given once, when it started, and this is the only thing that still knows it — so the script host asks rather than working it out, and a continuation of nothing answers nought.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Skip
member.summary: Cuts the line being spoken short and starts the next one.
member.returns: True when there was a line to cut short.

remarks.para: What a click during dialogue means. A player who has read the caption should not have to sit through the rest of the recording, and every adventure game of this kind lets them tap through — the original does not, which is a limitation of 1999 rather than a design anybody would choose.

The rest of the run is kept, because a conversation is a queue and skipping a line is not abandoning the exchange. Skipping the last line stops cleanly and lets whatever was waiting on the dialogue carry on, which is the same path the line finishing on its own takes.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Hush
member.summary: Stops whatever is being said and forgets the rest of it.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Quiet
member.summary: Stops the one-shot sounds, leaving the ambience and the dialogue.
member.remarks: What a script means by StopAllSounds. The room goes on sounding like the room and whoever is speaking goes on speaking; what stops is the door that was closing and the glass that was breaking.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Silence
member.summary: Stops everything, for leaving a room.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Leave
member.summary: Ends the room without ending what it sounds like.
member.remarks: Everything the room being left was saying belongs to that room and stops. What it sounded like does not: the next room's bed fades in over it, so leaving one place for another is heard as a change of place rather than as two cuts. If the next room names no ambience at all, this one fades out on its own — which is the same crossfade with nothing on the other side of it.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Fade(System.String,System.Nullable{GK3Reborn.Audio.AudioPlacement})

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Crossfade(System.Double)

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Stop(GK3Reborn.Formats.Audio.SoundtrackSound)
member.summary: Stops whatever was fading out.
Stops a soundtrack's sound the way the soundtrack says to.
member.param: The sound being stopped.
member.remarks: Only the voices this still holds — the ones that follow something. Everything else is a moment already over or nearly so, and the backend reclaims it.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Play(GK3Reborn.Formats.Audio.SoundtrackFile)
member.summary: Starts a soundtrack a script named, on top of the room's own.
member.param: The file.
member.returns: True if it was not already playing.
member.remarks: A script's soundtrack is another program running beside the room's rather than instead of it: PlaySoundTrack in the middle of a scene is a car arriving or a storm getting up, and the room is still the room underneath it. Playing one twice does nothing, which is what the original does — the same list started twice would be the same sound at two different points in its own walk.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.StopSoundtrack(System.String)
member.summary: Stops one soundtrack, or every soundtrack.
member.param: Which one, or null for all of them.
member.returns: How many were stopped.
member.remarks: The room's bed is left alone by name and stopped by "all", which is the difference between a script ending the storm it started and a script asking for silence.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Running
member.summary: The soundtracks the room is running, by name.
member.remarks: A room may be running several — RC1 at ten in the morning names a fountain, a room tone and birdsong — and most of them are silent at any given moment, because a soundtrack is mostly waiting. So this says what is running, where says what is sounding.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Placed(GK3Reborn.Formats.Animation.AnimationFile)
member.summary: Where a line is spoken from, or null when it belongs at the head.
member.param: The line's animation, which names its speaker in its caption.
member.returns: The placement, or null to centre it.
member.remarks: This line's own speaker rather than , which is the last one known: an animation with no caption names nobody, and taking the previous line's speaker would put an unattributed line wherever the last person to talk is standing.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.DialogueNear
member.summary: How near a speaker has to be before their voice stops getting louder.
member.remarks: A person talking is not a fountain: the useful range is a conversation's worth of room rather than a square's, so a line placed in the world is at full level for the few feet a conversation is held across and falls away beyond that. Wider than the game's own default for a sound, because a line the player cannot make out is worse than a line that is not quite placed right.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.DialogueFar
member.summary: And how far away it is as quiet as it gets.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Routing
member.summary: Which speakers are centred and which are placed in the room.
member.remarks: Gabriel by default, and everybody when the player turns on centred dialogue — which is an accessibility option, not a mixing preference (Plan/03 section 8).

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Soundtracks
member.summary: Reads a soundtrack by name, for the calls that name one.
member.remarks: A hook rather than an archive reference: a .STK is text in a barn, and the audio layer knowing how to open one would put the archives behind the mixer.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Where
member.summary: Where a model in the room is, for a sound that moves with it.
member.remarks: Follow=blk_sedan on a soundtrack's sound means the emitter travels with that model. Where the model is at any moment is the room's business rather than the audio's, so this is a hook: without one, a following sound stays where the file authored it, which is where the model starts.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Rising(System.Double)
member.summary: Brings the sounds that are fading in up to their own level.
member.remarks: Straight-line in gain, like the room-to-room crossfade beside it. A sound whose fade has finished is dropped from the list rather than kept and set to the same level every frame for as long as it plays.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Following
member.summary: Moves the sounds that travel with something.
member.remarks: Voices that have finished are dropped here rather than kept, because a room stood in for ten minutes starts a great many sounds and only a handful of them follow anything.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Update(System.Double)
member.summary: Starts the next line when the last one has finished.
member.remarks: Called once a frame. The device is the clock: a line is over when its source stops, not when a timer says it should have, so the two never drift apart.
member.param: How long since the last frame, for the crossfade.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio.Next
member.summary: Starts the line at the head of the queue.

member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneConditions
member.summary: Decides which of a scene file's conditional sections apply right now.

remarks.para: Almost everything in a SIF is conditional. R25 alone declares two beds, two states of the wardrobe, a hall backdrop that only exists on the first visit at 202P and a door that is there in every timeblock but one. Read without deciding those conditions a scene is the union of every state it can be in; deciding them is what turns it into a room.

The conditions are Sheep expressions in the section headers, the same language the action files use for their cases, so this is over the game's state rather than anything scene-specific. Across the 981 conditional headers in the corpus they call sixteen distinct functions, all of them state queries.

Results are cached per expression. The same header text repeats across sections and across the accessors that read them — models, actors, cameras and positions are four separate passes over one file — and the expressions must not be re-evaluated each time, both for cost and because a diagnostic would be raised once per pass.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneConditions.#ctor(GK3Reborn.Sheep.ISheepApi)
member.summary: Creates an evaluator.
member.param: Host used to resolve the functions a condition calls.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneConditions.Diagnostics
member.summary: Diagnostics raised while deciding.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneConditions.Applies
member.summary: The filter to read a scene file through.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneConditions.Holds(System.String)
member.summary: Whether a section's condition holds.
member.param: The expression, or null for an unconditional section.
member.returns: True when the section's lines count.
member.remarks: A malformed expression is reported and treated as false. The alternative — taking the section anyway — puts a scene into two states at once, which is the failure this class exists to remove.

member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition
member.summary: What a scene is, assembled from the one or two files that describe it.

remarks.para: A scene has a general initialisation file named for the location — R25.SIF — and may have a second named for the location and the timeblock together — R25202P.SIF. The general one describes the room: its geometry, its furniture, the cameras the player can stand at. The specific one describes what is happening in it that afternoon: Grace on the couch, Mosely and his bottle, the book, the dialogue cameras for the conversation they are about to have, and the action file that drives it.

Sixteen of R25's variants exist and none of their contents reaches the screen without this. Reading only the general file gives an empty hotel room at every point in a story that mostly happens in occupied ones.

The merge follows the original, which reads both files independently — each deciding its own conditions — and then joins the results, general first. Lists concatenate; the general block accumulates, with anything the specific file sets overriding what the general one said. Where the two name the same model the specific file wins, which falls out of the same last-declaration-wins rule that applies inside one file.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition.Models
member.summary: The models the scene places.
member.returns: The models, general file first.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition.Actors
member.summary: The actors the scene places.

remarks.para: Joined, but the ego is replaced rather than added to. A location's general file names the person whose game it usually is, and a timeblock file names the person whose game it is now: POU declares Gabriel and POU207A declares Grace, because on the second morning the tour is hers and he is somewhere else entirely.

Joining them outright put both in the room. Grace stood where the scene said and Gabriel stood at the origin with no spot of his own, in a scene he has no lines in and no business being in — and the room had two egos, which is one more than anything downstream expects. It is not a quirk of one scene: 157 scene and timeblock pairs across the corpus name Gabriel generally and Grace specifically, which is every Grace timeblock in every location she visits.
The same person is never placed twice either, for the reason the models are not: two copies of one character standing in one room is a worse answer than either of them.

Every camera the scene names, whatever kind it is.
member.remarks: For anything choosing between them rather than looking one up: the artists framed all three lists and a shot that holds a conversation may be in any of them.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition.InspectCameras
member.summary: The close-up views both files declare.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition.InspectCameraFor(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: The close-up view of a thing, if the scene declares one.
member.param: The noun the player clicked, or a model name.
The model standing behind that noun, if it is known.
member.returns: The camera, or null.
member.remarks: By noun first and by model second, which is the original's order. A noun is what the action file and the player agree on; a model is what the artists framed, and several scenes give the camera for a thing only under the name of the mesh drawn there.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition.AnyCameraNamed(System.String)
member.summary: Any camera the scene names, of whatever kind.
member.param: The camera's name.
member.returns: The camera, or null when the scene names none such.
member.remarks: What a script means by a camera angle: the original looks in every named list and complains if it finds nothing. Unlike this does not fall back to the default, because a script asking for a camera that is not there is a mistake worth hearing about rather than a reason to point the view somewhere else.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition.StartPosition(System.String)
member.summary: Where the player starts.
Where the player stands on walking into this room.
member.param: The location they came from, or null.
member.returns: The spot, or null when the scene names none and nothing should be guessed.

remarks.para: Never an arbitrary one. This used to fall back to the first entry of [POSITIONS], which put Gabriel wherever the file happened to list first — in the phone room that is EMILIO_HERE_1, a spot authored for somebody else and directly in front of the camera, so walking in filled the screen with the back of his head until the room's enter script moved him. 22 of the game's scene files reach this, and exactly one of the 102 that place a player defines a START at all, so the guess was doing nearly all of the work and doing it wrongly.

The artists' own convention answers it instead. A room names the spot you arrive at for each door into it, after where you came from: FR_LBY is where you stand having come from the lobby. 308 of them across 80 scenes. The room's enter script picks one by hand, and this is the same choice made a frame earlier, so the player never sees the wrong one.

Failing all that, nothing. An unplaced player stands at the origin until a script moves them, which is what the reference does and is a great deal better than standing somewhere the artists meant for a different person.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition.PositionNamed(System.String)
member.summary: A named spot, or null if neither file defines one under that name.
member.param: The spot's name.
member.returns: The position.
member.remarks: The timeblock file wins, since it is the one that both places an actor and says where — pos=GRACE_INIT and the GRACE_INIT spot are written together.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition.DefaultCamera
member.summary: The camera a scene opens on.
member.returns: The default camera, the first one, or null if neither file defines any.
member.remarks: From the general file. A timeblock file adds the cameras a cinematic cuts to and routinely declares an empty [ROOM_CAMERAS], so letting it answer here would open half the scenes in the game on nothing.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition.CameraNamed(System.String)
member.summary: Finds a camera by name, falling back to the scene's default.
member.param: Camera name, or null for the default.
member.returns: The camera, or null if the scene defines none.
member.remarks: A named lookup searches the cinematic cameras too. They are not viewpoints the player can occupy, but they are the angles the artists framed deliberately — the one looking out of R25's window, the three-shot over the couch — which makes them the useful ones to name when comparing a render against the original.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition.MergeActors
member.summary: The two files' model lists, joined by name.
member.remarks: The rule is the one that applies inside a single file, applied once more across the pair: with the conditions decided the last declaration wins outright, and without them a model is hidden only where every declaration agrees. See for why the two cases differ.
member.summary: Joins the two files' casts, with the timeblock's ego replacing the general one.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition.Dedupe(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GK3Reborn.Formats.Scenes.SceneActor})

member.summary: What the pointer is over and what can be done to it.
member.param: The thing itself, or null when the pointer is over nothing.
The verbs it answers to, here and now, most likely first.

What to call it on screen, when that is not its noun. Only the exits use it, and they need it: the artists numbered RC1's ways out EXIT, EXIT1 to EXIT5, in no order anybody could infer, and the interface was drawing "Exit3" at a player who has no way of knowing what three means.

member.summary: Whether there is anything to do.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.Hover.Default
member.summary: The verb a plain click performs.

remarks.para: The scene's own default when it names one — a door says OPEN — and otherwise the first verb the resolver offers, which is the order the action files put them in. Choosing for the player is the point: docs/screens.md and the brief both ask for one click to do the obvious thing, with the full list a right-click away, rather than the original's two-step through a verb ring.

Never the close-up. Looking at a thing is not doing something to it, and the close-up is offered for nearly every noun in the game — so while it counted, it won every click, coming out ahead of talking, opening and using. That is on the middle button now. Where a thing answers to nothing else, a left click means the same as a click on the floor and the player walks over.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.Hover.Closer
member.summary: The verb the middle button performs.
member.remarks: Whichever of the two close-up verbs is on offer — into a close-up, or back out of one. Null where the thing cannot be looked at closely, which leaves the button doing nothing rather than doing something else.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.Hover.IsCloseUp(System.String)
member.summary: Whether a verb is one of the two close-up verbs.

member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction
member.summary: Turns pointing at the room into doing something to it.

remarks.para: Three pieces already existed and nothing joined them up: says what is under a point on the screen, says what a noun answers to at this moment in the story, and performs the one that is chosen. This is the join, and it is deliberately thin — no state of its own, so that hovering can be asked every frame without ever changing anything.

Hovering must be free of consequences. It happens on every mouse move, and the resolver evaluates case conditions to answer, so anything that wrote to the story here would advance the game by moving the mouse across it.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Inspect
member.summary: The verb that looks closely at something, and the one that stops.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Undo
member.summary: Stops looking closely at something.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.WithInspect(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GK3Reborn.UI.Interaction.AvailableAction})
member.summary: Adds the close-up verb to what a thing answers to, and the way back out of it.
member.param: The thing under the pointer.
What the action files say about it.
member.returns: The same list, with at most one of the two close-up verbs on the front.

remarks.para: Both verbs are in VERBS.TXT and neither is in the action files: 40 rules in the corpus name INSPECT and none names INSPECT_UNDO, because the original engine put both on the bar itself rather than reading them — Scene::OnClicked adds one or the other to every noun it shows a bar for.

The way out is the part that was missing. Inspecting the register moved the view to a close-up of it and nothing could move it back: not walking away, not clicking elsewhere, and not leaving the room, so the phone room and every room after it opened pointing at a register that was not in them.

And neither verb is offered for something that cannot be looked at. Reported as "Inspect / Inspect Undo, and inspect didn't even inspect": the close-up was offered for every noun in the game, most of which no scene declares a camera for, so choosing it moved nothing — and because it still counted as having happened, the menu then offered to undo the thing that had not occurred. is asked first, and it can now frame a close-up from the object's own bounds, so what is refused here is only what has no geometry at all.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Carrying
member.summary: What the player has to use on things.
member.remarks: An action file writes "use the wallet on Buthane" as a rule whose verb is WALLET, so an item in the bag is a verb the world answers to and an item that is not is a verb nobody may choose. Offering all of them regardless is offering the player every puzzle's solution as a menu item from the first room.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Called(System.String,GK3Reborn.Game.Interaction.ScenePick,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GK3Reborn.UI.Interaction.AvailableAction})
member.summary: What to call a thing whose noun is not worth showing.
member.param: What the scene calls it.
The thing itself, for the default verb its model declares.
What it answers to, for when the model declares no verb.
member.returns: A better name, or null to use the noun.
member.remarks: Only the numbered exits, and the name comes out of the game's own data: the rule behind the door says where it goes and turns that into what the place is called.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Numbered(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: A hotel door, called by its number rather than by who is behind it.
member.param: The noun the scene gives it.
The model's own name, which carries the room number.
member.returns: The label, or null when this is not a numbered door.

remarks.para: The second floor names its doors after the guests: EMILIOS_DOOR, BUTHANES_DOOR, WILKES_DOOR. Shown as they are, the corridor introduces every suspect in the hotel the first time Gabriel walks down it, before he has met any of them — a whole evening of the game's own pacing given away by a hover label.

The number is what is actually on the door, and the scene agrees: beside each one it places a R27_PLATE the player can read. So the label is the number, which is true at every point in the story and spoils nothing. The name is not withheld and then revealed — knowing that room 27 is Emilio's is something the player works out and then keeps, and a label that changed under them would be its own small lie.

Taken from the model's name — hal_27_door_scene, hal_door_29, hal_21door — rather than from a table, because a table of eight doors in one corridor is a thing to keep in step with the data by hand. A door whose model names no number is left alone; the supply closet has none and wants none.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.OneOfSeveral(System.String)
member.summary: One of several copies of a thing, called by what the thing is.
member.param: The noun the scene gives it.
member.returns: The name without its copy number, or null when the number belongs.

remarks.para: The church carves the four angels as four objects — FOUR_ANGELS1 through FOUR_ANGELS4 — and pointing at one of them read "Four Angels4", which is the data's bookkeeping showing through the interface.

A trailing number is not always bookkeeping. BUZZER_RM25 and DUMB_WAITER_LOCK_R21 end in digits that are room numbers and mean everything; trimming those gives "Buzzer Rm". What tells the two apart is whether the scene also declares the name without the number — the church declares FOUR_ANGELS beside its four, and no room declares a BUZZER_RM. So the data answers it, and no list of exceptions has to be kept in step with the corpus by hand.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Strings
member.summary: What the game's own names for things are, when anything read them.
member.remarks: Settable rather than read here, because the archives belong to the launcher and this is built per room. Left alone it knows nothing and every numbered exit is called "Exit", which is still better than a number.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Introductions
member.summary: Who the player has been introduced to, when anything read the table.
member.remarks: Left alone it says everybody, which is what the interface did before this and what a test that only cares about verbs wants.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Watcher
member.summary: The room as it stands, for questions only it can answer.
member.remarks: Whether a thing can be looked at closely depends on where it is and what it occupies, which is the live room's business rather than the action files'. Optional: without one the close-up verb is offered as it always was, which is what the tests that build an interaction with no room expect.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Nouns

member.returns: Each noun once, with the middle of what it occupies in world space.
member.remarks: For showing them all at once while a key is held. It asks the picker, so what it lists is exactly what a click could reach — a label for something unclickable would be worse than no label.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Labelled(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: What a noun is called when there is no pointer resting on it.
member.param: What the scene calls it.
The object it was found on, which carries a door's number.
member.returns: The label.
member.remarks: The same answers gives, less the one that needs a pick: a numbered exit is named after where its verb's script goes, and showing every door in the room at once has no verb to ask about. Routing them through here matters because the point of showing every hotspot at once is a corridor full of them, which is exactly where a label that gives too much away does the most damage.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.ModelOf(System.String)
member.summary: The scene's own model for a noun, when it places one.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Stranger(System.String)
member.summary: What to call somebody the player has not been introduced to.
member.param: The noun the scene gives them.
member.returns: What they look like, or null when the player already knows their name.

remarks.para: A scene names its people by their surnames — BUTHANE, BUCHELLI, WILKES — and the original never had to care, because it drew no label. This one does, so pointing at the woman waiting by the tour bus told the player her name before Gabriel had said a word to her. It is the leak the second-floor doors had, somewhere there is no room number to fall back on.

So the label says what can actually be seen. "Woman" and "Man" come out of the character's own ShoeType in CHARACTERS.TXT — the only thing in the shipped data that says which is which — rather than out of a table kept here by hand, and decides when the name is earned using the action files' own MET_ conditions.

Anybody the file says nothing about keeps their name, and so does anybody the character file has no shoes for. Both failures are the same shape and it is the safe one: a name a little early is a small spoiler, and a stranger who stays a stranger after two days of conversation is a bug the player cannot get round.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.Do(GK3Reborn.Game.Hover,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Does something to what is under the pointer.
member.param: What was under it, from .
Which verb, or null for the default one.
Whether the player asked twice. A double-click means the same thing as a click and means it more urgently, so the walk in front of the action is run rather than walked.
member.returns: What happened, or null when there was nothing to do.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneInteraction.FloorTarget(GK3Reborn.Game.Hover)
member.summary: Where a click would send the player, when it landed on the floor and nothing else.
member.param: What was under the pointer, from .
member.returns: A spot to walk to, or null when the click was not a click on open floor.

remarks.para: The room's floor is one named object among a hundred and the scene says which — the same floor= line reads for heights. So a floor click is a pick that reached that object and nothing nearer: a rug, a bed or a doorway standing in front of it is a click on the rug, the bed or the doorway, which is what the original does and what the player means.

The answer is the nearest spot the boundary allows rather than the point itself. The floor mesh runs under the furniture and out through the doorways, so aiming at where the ray landed would send an actor into a wardrobe; the boundary is the authority on where a person may stand and it puts them against it instead. A point out of reach still walks — gets as near as the floor allows — because getting closer beats refusing to move.

The clicked height is kept while the boundary decides the ground plan, because the boundary is a bitmap seen from above and has no storeys: on a staircase its answer alone cannot say which of the two floors above one another was meant.
