member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader
member.summary: Assembles a scene the way the game does.

remarks.para: A scene is not one file. The initialisation file names a scene asset for the time of day; the scene asset names the geometry, the objects in it and the lights that lit it; the geometry references textures and pairs surface for surface with a lightmap set. This walks that chain and puts the result on the GPU.

Conditional sections are taken at face value. Which apply depends on the story's state, and deciding that needs the Sheep virtual machine and a running game; until then, showing everything a scene can contain is more useful than showing nothing.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader._nearTrees
member.summary: Which of a room's trees the budget stretched to growing in full.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader._standing
member.summary: Where a prop has already put a modelled tree, so the room does not too.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.#ctor(GK3Reborn.Content.GameArchives,System.Action{System.String})
member.summary: Creates a loader.
member.param: Where to read assets from.
Optional progress sink.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Enhanced
member.summary: Higher-resolution textures to use in place of the archives', if there are any.
member.remarks: A layer rather than a replacement: a texture with no enhanced version loads from the archive as before, so a partial set works. Null or empty means the game looks exactly as it shipped.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Normals
member.summary: Generated normal maps, standing beside the colour textures.
member.remarks: A separate set from because they are a separate pass and a separate judgement: a surface may have a better colour texture and no normal map, or the other way round. Named for the colour texture they belong to.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Orms
member.summary: Generated occlusion, roughness and metalness, packed into one picture per surface.
member.remarks: Red, green and blue in that order, which is the glTF packing every generator and every authoring tool already writes. A separate set again, and a separate judgement: a roughness that reads as wet stone is a different mistake from a normal map that embosses printed lettering, and they are reviewed apart.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Heights
member.summary: Generated height fields, one per surface, for parallax.
member.remarks: Mid grey is the modelled surface. Consumed as a texture-coordinate offset rather than as displacement, so it deepens what is already flat and changes no silhouette.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Trees
member.summary: Modelled trees to stand in place of the scene's flat foliage cards.
member.remarks: The one enhancement here that changes geometry rather than what is painted on it, and it is confined to foliage because foliage is where a card is the whole of the object: a wall drawn flat is a wall, and a tree drawn flat is a picture of a tree. Null or empty leaves every card exactly as it shipped.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.TerrainDirectory
member.summary: Where the reconstructed terrain sets live loose, or null for none.
member.remarks: Flat files named <set>.<part>.<ext> — BMB_A.heights.r32, BMB_A.splat.png — written by PbrLab/publish_terrain.py. A loose file beats the packed one, the same rule every other enhanced kind follows. A scene whose sky has no set anywhere keeps its painted horizon. See ContentWorkspace/enhanced/skyboxes/terrain-plan.md for the contract.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Finishes
member.summary: What the material library measured about each texture, or null to displace only the floor.
member.remarks: Only consulted to widen relief displacement outdoors: which of a scene's textures carry a displaced-class finish is a question the sink's own copy could answer, but the sink learns of surfaces one batch at a time and the relief plan wants the whole set before the first one.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.TerrainPacks
member.summary: The ReBarn packs the terrain sets ship in, or null for none.
member.remarks: The same files as , as Raw entries under their flat names. This is what makes the reconstructed horizon part of the shipped game rather than a workspace-only extra.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.TreesGrown
member.summary: How many flat cards were replaced by a modelled tree in the last load.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Compressed
member.summary: The same textures and maps, block-compressed, if the pipeline has built them.

remarks.para: A fallback rather than a preference, and deliberately so while the enhanced sets are still being generated. A .dds in build is whatever the last compression run made of whatever the enhanced set held at the time; the .png beside it is what the generator has produced now. Taking the compressed one first means regenerating a texture changes nothing on screen until somebody remembers to recompress, which is a debugging session nobody enjoys twice.

The trade it wins — nothing to decode, a mip chain already built, a quarter of the video memory — is a shipping concern rather than a development one, and it comes back the moment the enhanced sets stop moving.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.FlatSurfaces
member.summary: Colour only: no normal maps, no finishes, no height, from any source.
member.remarks: --flat, for photographing what the maps alone are doing.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.SmoothHeads
member.summary: How many times to subdivide a character's head; zero draws it as authored.
member.remarks: Characters only, and only their heads. See for why that is the one part of a GK3 character which can be re-meshed at all.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Glances
member.summary: Who is looking at what as the scene is built.
member.remarks: A glance is applied where an actor is placed, because a character has no skeleton and turning a head means placing one of its meshes differently. Live glancing — somebody turning to watch you cross the room — needs an update loop that does not exist yet; this is the same mechanism, decided once.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.EnhancedTexturesUsed
member.summary: How many textures came from the enhanced set rather than the archives.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Load(GK3Reborn.Rendering.ISceneSink,System.String,System.String,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Loads a scene into geometry.
member.param: Where to put it.
Scene name, such as R25.
Time of day: M, A, E or N.
Receives anything that could not be loaded.
member.returns: What was loaded, or null if the scene has no geometry at all.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Load(GK3Reborn.Rendering.ISceneSink,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Loads a scene at a point in the story.
member.param: Where to put it.
What to load, and when in the story.
Receives anything that could not be loaded.
member.returns: What was loaded, or null if the scene has no geometry at all.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Daylight(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest,System.String,GK3Reborn.Formats.Scenes.SceneAssetFile)
member.summary: What hour to put the sun at for a room that has a sky over it.
member.param: What was asked for, which usually carries the story's clock.
The timeblock or asset suffix the caller named, if any.
The scene asset that was chosen.
member.returns: The hour to light the room at.

remarks.para: A sky means a sun. There is always an answer here, and that is the point: the rule used to be "a sky and a timeblock", so a room entered without one was lit flat, cast no shadows at all, and looked like a bug in the renderer rather than a missing argument. Whether the hour has a sun in it is 's business — it answers null at night, which is a sun's absence for a reason.

The story's own clock first. Then whatever the caller named, which is how a headless render asks for a particular hour. Then the asset's own suffix, which is the artists saying what time of day the room was baked for: _M morning, _A afternoon, _E evening, _N night. That is a real answer and not a guess — it is the same letter that chose the lightmaps the room is already lit by, so the sun agrees with the bake by construction.
And mid-morning when even that is silent, because a room with a sky and no other evidence is a daylit room.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Compose(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Assembles what a scene is, without loading anything that has to be drawn.
member.param: Which scene, and where the story is.
Receives loading diagnostics.
member.returns: The scene, or null if it has no initialisation file at all.
member.remarks: The composition — which state the room is in, who is in it, where they may stand, what may be done to them — is decided entirely by text files, and answering questions about it does not need the fifty megabytes of geometry and the hundred textures that go with drawing it. A sweep of the whole corpus is the case that makes the difference worth having: 1,343 pairs at a few milliseconds each rather than at a second each.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.CameraFor(GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,GK3Reborn.Rendering.ISceneSink,System.String)
member.summary: Builds a camera from one of a scene's own viewpoints.
member.param: The loaded scene.
Its geometry, for a fallback framing.
Which camera, or null for the scene's default.
member.returns: The camera.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.CameraAt(GK3Reborn.Formats.Scenes.SceneCamera,GK3Reborn.Rendering.ISceneSink)
member.summary: Builds the view one of the scene's cameras describes.
member.param: Where it stands and which way it points.
The room, for how far the far plane has to reach.
member.returns: The view.
member.remarks: Separate from the lookup because not every camera in a scene has a name: the close-up views are keyed by what they look at rather than called anything.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.HiddenObjects(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition)
member.summary: Objects baked into the geometry that must not be drawn.
member.remarks: Hit tests are volumes the player can click but never see — a doorway's clickable region, the area a note occupies on a desk. They are ordinary geometry inside the BSP with an ordinary texture, so nothing about the geometry itself says to skip them; only the initialisation file does. Drawing them puts large flat slabs through the middle of a room, which is exactly what the lobby showed before this.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.FloorTextures(GK3Reborn.Formats.Scenes.BspFile,System.String)
member.summary: The textures on the object the scene calls its floor.
member.remarks: Not a guess and not a matter of what a texture is called. Every scene's general .SIF names one floor= object, the BSP knows which surfaces belong to it, and each surface names its texture — the same chain the walk height query follows. Sixty-nine scenes name a floor and a hundred and twenty-six distinct textures are on one; TE3FLOORCRS is a floor and 27FLOOR is not.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.ReportDisputedVisibility(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Notes the models drawn only because their condition could not be decided.
member.remarks: These are shown rather than hidden, so a wrong guess adds an object instead of removing one. Naming them is what makes the guess reviewable: without this the only evidence is an object that looks out of place, which is hard to trace back here.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.ReadBehaviour(System.String,System.String,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Reads a behaviour script — what something does when nobody is asking it to.
member.param: The script's file name, or null.
What it belongs to, for a diagnostic.
Receives what could not be read.
member.returns: The script, or null when there is none or it is missing.

remarks.para: A script whose every instruction is not understood is kept now. It did not used to be, and the reason was good at the time: the branching half of the language decides which idle to play, so running only the parts that were understood picked the wrong one and repeated it for as long as the scene was loaded.

That half is understood now — ONEOF above all, which is 1,559 of the corpus's instructions — so what is left unread is the perception layer: WHENNEAR and its relatives, which add a way for a script to be interrupted rather than deciding what it does. A script missing those does the right things and misses a cue, which is much better than a character standing still.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.IsBakedIn(GK3Reborn.Formats.Scenes.SceneModel)
member.summary: Whether a model refers to geometry inside the BSP rather than a file.
member.remarks: Only prop and gasprop load a model file; everything else names an object the geometry already contains. Loading a file for those draws the same furniture twice, in slightly different places, which reads as z-fighting rather than as a loading mistake.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.ReadBoundary(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Reads the bitmap that says where actors may stand.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.ReadCameraBounds(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Reads the shells that fence the camera into the room.
member.remarks: A scene that names none, or names one no archive holds, gets no bounds and a camera that can go anywhere — which is what every scene did before this and is a great deal better than a room the camera cannot move in. The names are model files rather than objects in the geometry: nothing draws them, and only this reads them.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.ReadDefinition(System.String,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Reads the one or two initialisation files that describe a scene.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Candidates(System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Names to try, most specific first.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.WoodBudget
member.summary: How many triangles of grown wood one room may be given.
member.remarks: A cap rather than a target, and a guard rather than a constraint: no room in the corpus comes near it now that a card is counted as the face an artist drew rather than as the pieces a BSP splitter left. It is kept because the arithmetic that motivated it is still true — a stand of a hundred and sixty trees at four thousand triangles each is six hundred thousand triangles of scenery behind a conversation, in a room that shipped at six — and because a scene nobody has looked at yet should not be able to spend that. Every stand is grown at the far detail first, which is a quarter of the cost, and the budget left over is spent raising the tallest trees to full.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.GrowWoods(GK3Reborn.Formats.Scenes.BspFile,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Finds the stands of trees in a room, as far as the budget reaches.
member.param: The parsed room.
Receives a warning for any grown tree that will not load.
member.returns: The objects whose cards are to be replaced, largest first.
member.remarks: All of an object or none of it. A room is hidden by name and there is no way to hide half of one, so growing part of a stand and leaving the rest would draw the modelled trees over the cards they were meant to replace.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Readable(GK3Reborn.Game.Foliage.FoliageObject,GK3Reborn.Content.TreeLibrary,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Whether every tree a stand needs can actually be loaded.
member.remarks: Both details, because the budget decides between them after this and either may be asked for. A stand is all or nothing: the room hides its cards by object name, so one tree that will not read costs the whole object rather than one trunk.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.PlantWoods(GK3Reborn.Rendering.ISceneSink,System.Collections.Generic.List{GK3Reborn.Game.Foliage.FoliageObject},GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Stands the grown trees where a room's cards were.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.AlreadyStanding(GK3Reborn.Game.TreeSite)
member.summary: Whether a prop has already grown a tree where this site is.

remarks.para: A third of a crown's radius, which is much tighter than it sounds and is a measured number rather than a cautious one. Where a scene places a foliage prop, the room's own copy of that tree is within twenty-two units of it and usually within five — measured across WOD's eighteen pines, whose crowns are two hundred units across. So the duplicates are unambiguous, and anything further away is a different tree.

The looser rule this replaced took a whole radius, which suppressed 81 of WOD's 87 stands to remove 18 duplicates: the hillside behind the eighteen props went with them, and the wood came out as a clearing.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.GrowTree(GK3Reborn.Formats.Models.ModFile,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Grows a modelled tree in place of a prop that is only a picture of one.
member.param: The prop as the archive holds it.
Receives a warning when a grown tree will not read.
member.returns: The tree and where it stands, or null when this prop stays as it is.

remarks.para: Null is the ordinary answer and costs one dictionary lookup per submesh: no tree library, no foliage texture, or a prop that is a tree and something else all leave the card alone. That matters because this runs over every prop in every scene, and most scenes are indoors.

A tree that will not read leaves the card too, rather than leaving a gap. Enhanced content is a draft until somebody has looked at it, and one bad file in a set should cost that tree and nothing else.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.PlaceActors(GK3Reborn.Rendering.ISceneSink,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag,System.String)
member.summary: Puts the scene's actors where the scene says they stand.

remarks.para: The models are in their bind pose. Actors are animated by GAS scripts driving ACT animations against a skeleton, none of which exists yet, so an actor standing here is standing exactly as the artist modelled them rather than idling.

Everyone the section names is loaded, whatever else the line says, and the two exceptions this used to make were the same mistake twice — the one already recorded above about RC1's moped, made again about people.

An actor with no pos= was being skipped outright. 206 actor/timeblock pairs in the corpus have none, and they are not absent: GKActor::Init only declines to set a position, and what places them is their initanim= or the script that walks them in. Emilio is one of them in the lobby at 110A, so the room's only other person was never there — and when the story sent him out through the front door, all that arrived in the square was a door swinging by itself.

An actor declared hidden was being skipped too, and hidden is where several of them start: RC1 hides Emilio while he is still indoors and the animation that walks him out turns him back on. A model that was never read cannot be shown.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Sides
member.summary: The cube map's sides, in the order the hardware wants them.
member.remarks: Front is +X and right is +Z, not the other way about. Measured off the images rather than reasoned from the names, twice and independently. Butting each side's right-hand column against each other side's left-hand column, the four that join are left→back→right→front, with a mean difference of 2.9 to 6.1 against 23 to 34 for every other pairing. Butting each side's top row against the four edges of the up face agrees: front meets +X, right meets +Z, back meets −X and left meets −Z, at 2.9 to 3.2 against 25 to 48.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.LoadSkybox(GK3Reborn.Rendering.ISceneSink,GK3Reborn.Formats.Scenes.SkyboxDefinition,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Gives the room its sky, when the scene asset names one.

remarks.para: The six sides go to the device in the order the hardware wants — right, left, up, down, front, back — which is not the order the file lists them in.

A missing side is filled with one that is present, as the original does: the ground is usually left out because nothing can see it, but the hardware still requires six. A sky whose sides are different sizes is refused rather than resampled, because nothing in the corpus has one and guessing would hide a misreading.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.TerrainSetName(GK3Reborn.Formats.Scenes.SkyboxDefinition)
member.summary: The set a sky's faces belong to: BMB_A_512RT names BMB_A.
member.param: The scene's sky.
member.returns: The set name, or null when the faces follow no known convention.

member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.TerrainMeta
member.summary: What the offline pipeline wrote beside each heightfield.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.TerrainMeta.#ctor(System.Int32,System.Single)
member.summary: What the offline pipeline wrote beside each heightfield.

member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.TerrainTree
member.summary: One tree of the backdrop's forest, as the offline placement wrote it.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.TerrainTree.#ctor(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: One tree of the backdrop's forest, as the offline placement wrote it.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.ReadTerrainPart(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: One part of a terrain set: the loose file first, then the packs.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.TerrainTile(System.String,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: One of the terrain's ground tiles: enhanced first, the archives after.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.NormalMapsUsed
member.summary: How many surfaces in the last scene were given a normal map.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.OrmMapsUsed
member.summary: How many were given an occlusion/roughness/metalness map.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.HeightMapsUsed
member.summary: How many were given a height map.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.CompressedUsed
member.summary: How many of the last scene's textures came from the compressed set.

member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Source
member.summary: Where a texture came from, for the counts a load reports.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Source.Original
member.summary: The archives, as the game shipped.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Source.Enhanced
member.summary: A higher-resolution PNG.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Source.Compressed
member.summary: A block-compressed DDS.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.Decoders
member.summary: How many textures are decoded at once.
member.remarks: Bounded well below the core count on purpose. Each decode in flight holds about 33 MB — the compressed file, the inflated rows and the pixels — so the ceiling here is what the load costs in memory at its peak, and past a point the machine is waiting on memory bandwidth rather than on arithmetic.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.LoadTextures(GK3Reborn.Rendering.ISceneSink,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String},System.String,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Reads, decodes and uploads the textures a room asks for.

remarks.para: In three passes rather than one, because the middle one is worth spreading over the machine. Deciding what is missing has to be in order — asking the sink what it holds is not something two threads may do at once, and the answer counts what was reused — and uploading has to be in order because that is the device. Decoding is neither: it is pure arithmetic over bytes nobody else is looking at.

It is also nearly all of the time. An enhanced texture is 2048², which is 48 ms and 33 MB of decode apiece, and a room wants dozens of them with a normal map each; done one after another that is ten seconds of a scene load with thirty-one cores idle.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.ReadActions(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Brings the scene's action files into scope.
member.remarks: The files decide what the player may do to a noun, so this is what turns a click that resolves to NIGHTSTAND into a list of verbs. Which files apply is ' business; this reads them and hands them to a resolver sharing the story host the scene's own conditions were decided through, because two hosts over the same state would sooner or later give two answers.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.ReadSoundtracks(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneDefinition,GK3Reborn.Foundation.Diagnostics.DiagnosticBag)
member.summary: Reads the soundtracks a scene names.
member.remarks: A soundtrack is a little script rather than a piece of music — wait a second, play the room's theme, wait five to ten seconds, play a mood — so a scene that names one and never reads it knows nothing about what the room sounds like. Reading it is cheap and separate from playing it, which needs a clock and an audio device.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneLoader.TurnedHead(System.String,GK3Reborn.Formats.Models.ModFile,GK3Reborn.Formats.Scenes.ScenePosition)
member.summary: Where an actor's head should be pointing, if they are looking at anything.
member.remarks: Null unless somebody has asked. A character with nothing to look at stands as the artist modelled them, which is what every actor in the game has done until now.

member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest
member.summary: A scene to load, and the point in the story to load it at.

remarks.para: The timeblock a caller names can mean one of two things, and the difference matters. 202P is a point in the story: the scene file's conditions can be decided against it, so the scene comes out in exactly one state, with the right bed made, the right door in place and the right asset and bake chosen by the file itself. A is only the suffix on an asset name — several timeblocks share one afternoon bake — so it picks geometry and lighting and says nothing about the story.

Both are useful. The suffix form is how a tool asks to see a scene's afternoon lighting without inventing a story state to justify it, and it is what the render tooling has always taken. Naming no timeblock at all leaves the conditions undecided and loads the union of every state the scene can be in, which is the right answer for a corpus survey and the wrong one for a game.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest.Scene
member.summary: The scene's name, which is also its three-letter location code.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest.AssetSuffix
member.summary: The M/A/E/N suffix to prefer, if the caller gave one.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest.State
member.summary: The story state, when the caller named a real timeblock.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest.TimeblockCode
member.summary: The timeblock's code, which is half the name of the scene's second file.
member.remarks: A scene may have a file named for the location and the timeblock together — R25202P.SIF — holding what is happening in the room rather than what the room is. Null when the caller gave only an asset suffix: A covers seven timeblocks and names none of them.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest.Conditions
member.summary: The evaluator to read the scene file through, when there is a state.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest.Api
member.summary: The script host the conditions are decided through, when there is a state.
member.remarks: Shared with whatever else has to ask the story a question while the scene stands — the action files, above all, whose cases are Sheep expressions over the same state. Giving them a second host would give them a second answer.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest.Continuing(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,System.String)
member.summary: A request for the next room, in a story that is already under way.
member.param: The host the story has been running against.
Where the player is going.
member.returns: The request.

remarks.para: starts a story; this continues one. The difference is the whole point of walking through a door: a new state would forget everything the player has done, and a new host would forget every function the last room registered and every script it had loaded.

The arrival is not recorded here. A scene file asks GetEgoCurrentLocationCount() < 1 to mean "the first time here", so while the file is being read the count still has to be the number of previous visits; the scripts that run once the room is standing ask for one instead. Counting the arrival first satisfies the scripts and not the file, and the two disagreeing is how RC1 came to play Gabriel's line about Wilkes's moped over a square with no moped in it — the scene had already decided not to place it. See , which the caller runs once the room is up.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneRequest.For(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Reads a timeblock argument.
member.param: Scene name, such as R25.
A story timeblock such as 202P, an asset suffix such as N, or null.
member.returns: The request.

member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting
member.summary: The script functions that need a scene rather than a story.

remarks.para: Most of what a script asks about is the story — flags, counts, who is carrying what — and lives on for as long as the game does. A few questions are about the room the player is standing in and mean nothing outside it: whether the van parked across the road is in the way. Those are registered here, against one loaded scene, and go when it does.

Three families so far. The walkers, because a boundary is painted once, before anybody knows where the van will park, so the scripts move things onto and off the floor as the story goes. And the cameras, because a camera angle is a name the scene gives — OPEN_WARDROBE, LONG_FROM_STAIRS — and means nothing in the next room. And the glances, because who somebody is looking at is a fact about a room with both of them in it.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Attach(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,GK3Reborn.Game.Actors.Glances,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate,System.Func{System.String,GK3Reborn.Formats.Animation.GasFile})
member.summary: Registers a scene's own functions on a host.
member.param: The host.
The scene they act on.
Where to record who is looking at what, if anywhere.
The room's audio, or null to leave the sound calls recorded.
What moves actors, or null to leave the walking calls recorded.
Where a behaviour script named by another one is read from, or null to leave the fidget calls recorded. Only a caller with the archives can answer it.
member.remarks: Call it again for the next scene: the functions close over this one, and the last registration wins, which is what changing rooms means.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Conversing(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate)
member.summary: Pointing the camera at one of the angles the scene names.

remarks.para: Three ways to ask, and the difference between them is the player's. A plain cut happens only if the player has left cinematics on, or a script has temporarily insisted; a forced cut ignores both, because some things the story has to show. A glide is a cut that should take a moment, and until there is a clock to take it in, it arrives at the same place — the angle it ends at is the observable part, and the travelling is not.

A camera the scene does not name is reported rather than ignored. The original logs it too, and it is worth hearing: a script pointing the view at nothing leaves the player looking at whatever they were looking at before, which reads as the game having missed its cue.

member.summary: Makes a conversation change what its participants do while it lasts.
member.param: The host, which keeps the story's own record of it.
The room, which owns the actors and their scripts.
member.remarks: Registered over the state-only pair on the host, rather than instead of them: a console, a tool or a save being replayed still has to be able to say a conversation is on without a room to hold it in. What this adds is the room's half — the [LISTENERS] scripts and the poses that go with them.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Asking(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene)
member.summary: Questions a script asks about what is in the room.
member.param: The host.
The room.
member.remarks: All three were unanswered, and an unanswered question is worse than an unperformed instruction: a script branches on the answer, so a silent zero sends it down the wrong path and everything after that is wrong for a reason nothing records.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.AttachGlances(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,GK3Reborn.Game.Actors.Glances)
member.summary: Turning a head to look at something.

remarks.para: The reference implementation registers all of these and every one of them is an empty body that returns zero, so no character in that build has ever glanced at anything. They are not switched off; they were never written.

What they need is unusual and, as it turns out, easier than a skeleton would be. GK3's people are a dozen separate meshes with their own transforms, so turning a head is placing one mesh differently, about the mesh's own origin — which is where the neck is. finds which mesh that is from what it is painted with, since the format has no room for a name.

The duration each of these carries is not obeyed yet: a glance arrives where it is going rather than easing there, because easing needs a clock and an update loop. The Quick forms are recorded as such so that when there is one, the difference between a snap and a turn is already in the data.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Where(GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,System.String)
member.summary: Where something in the scene is, for an actor to look at.
member.remarks: The middle of it rather than its feet: an actor looking at another looks at their head, and one looking at a wardrobe looks at the middle of the wardrobe.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Middle(GK3Reborn.Game.PlacedModel)
member.summary: The middle of a placed model, in world space.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Extent(GK3Reborn.Game.PlacedModel)
member.summary: How far a placed model reaches, where it is now standing.
member.param: The model.
member.returns: Its corners, or null when it has no geometry at all.
member.remarks: The same walk as , kept beside it: seeing something is a question about the whole of it rather than about its centre, which for a car, a bookcase or a bed is inside the thing and never visible from anywhere.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Heading(GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,System.String)
member.summary: Which way an actor is facing, from the spot the scene stood them on.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Footprint(GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,System.String)
member.summary: The ground a named object stands on, as a rectangle.
member.remarks: A box around everything the object is made of, flattened onto the floor by throwing the height away — the original does the same, and it is coarse in the right direction: an actor walks around a chair rather than through the gap under its seat. The name may be a prop standing in the room or an object baked into the geometry, because the scene files name both the same way.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Bounds(GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,System.String)
member.summary: The box round everything named that, whether it is a prop or part of the room.
member.remarks: The scene files name both the same way, so both are looked for. Height matters where a footprint does not: an actor looking at a ceiling fan looks up at it, and one told to look at the floor of a wardrobe looks down.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Speak(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneAudio,GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate)
member.summary: Makes the calls that were recorded actually make a sound.
member.param: The host.
The room's audio.
The room, for the cameras a conversation may be watched from.
Where the speakers are standing.
member.remarks: These were all registered as recorded — the presentation surface named but not performed — because there was no device and no decoder. There is both now, so they are registered over. A call whose sound cannot be found still returns cleanly: a missing footstep should not stop the script that stepped.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Watching(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate)
member.summary: Points the camera at whoever is about to talk.
member.param: The game, for who is speaking to whom.
The room, for the cameras it names.
Where the speakers are standing.

remarks.para: Three answers, in order. The conversation's own initial camera where the scene names one; the camera a script asked for with SetDefaultDialogueCamera; and otherwise whichever of the scene's cameras best holds both speakers — see .

The third is the port's own decision rather than the original's. It has to be: SetDefaultDialogueCamera does nothing in the reference and the lobby's introduction to Emilio names no conversation at all, so there is no authored answer for it — and the exchange was playing out with the camera pointed across an empty room. Nothing is invented: the choice is between shots the artists framed.
Only once per exchange, and never while cinematics are off — that switch exists so a player can stop the camera taking itself off them, and this is exactly the kind of cut it means.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Named(GK3Reborn.Formats.Scenes.SceneCamera,System.String)
member.summary: Whether a dialogue camera belongs to a conversation.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Speakers(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate)
member.summary: Where the people in a conversation are standing.
member.remarks: The player and whatever they are talking to, which is what an action is about — a topic is EMILIO:T_INTRODUCE and the two of them are the exchange. Anybody the room does not have is left out rather than guessed at, and a conversation with only one findable speaker still gets a shot that holds them.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Looking(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate)
member.summary: Which way the people in a conversation are facing.
member.remarks: In the same order gives them, and zero for anybody whose facing nothing can answer — a zero vector is skipped rather than believed, so an unknown facing costs a shot nothing.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Walking(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate)
member.summary: Makes the walking calls move somebody.
member.param: The host.
The room being crossed.
What moves them.

remarks.para: Both forms take a name and mean different things by it. WalkTo names a spot the scene declares — TO_B25, the patch of floor in front of the bathroom door — and WalkToSee names a model, meaning walk until you can see it. Seeing is not worked out yet, so it walks to the model instead, which is the same answer for anything in the open and too close for anything behind something else.
These say how long they take through , so a waited walk holds up the line of dialogue that follows it rather than being spoken over on the way.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Distance(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GK3Reborn.Sheep.SheepValue},System.Int32)
member.summary: The radius an argument asks about, in scene units.
member.remarks: A negative one is a mistake in the data rather than a very small circle; the original refuses it outright and so does this, which is what the zero means.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Near(GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,System.Nullable{System.Numerics.Vector3},System.String,System.Single)
member.summary: Whether a point is within a distance of one of the scene's named spots.
member.remarks: Flat, on the ground plan. The spots carry a height and several of them are authored at zero against a floor that is not, so a distance through the vertical would answer "far away" about somebody standing on the mark.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Send(GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate,System.String,System.String,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Starts a walk or a turn, and says how long it will take.

remarks.para: Arriving facing the right way is most of what a walk is for. A scene's named spots carry a heading — the way somebody standing there is meant to face — and walking to look at something means ending up looking at it. Without either, an actor arrives facing whichever way the last corner of the route pointed, which is usually a wall.
A turn goes nowhere. 394 of the corpus's approaches are TurnToModel, and walking to the thing instead puts the actor on top of what they meant to look at.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.ToAnimationStart(GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate,System.String,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Walks an actor to the spot an animation expects them to start from.
member.remarks: Nothing happens if the animation moves nobody by that name, which is the right answer: an approach=anim naming a scenery animation has nobody to walk, and refusing to run the action because of it would lose the action as well as the walk.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Approach(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate,System.String,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Aiming)
member.summary: Stops an actor short of the thing they were sent to.
member.remarks: The distance is the character's own WalkerHeight out of CHARACTERS.TXT — Gabriel is 76 units — which agrees with what the artists did where they placed an approach spot by hand: the few in the corpus that name both a thing and a position stand 68 to 184 units off it. See for why walking to the middle is not good enough.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Modelled(GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,System.String)
member.summary: The model name behind whichever of an actor's two names a script used.
member.param: The room, which is what knows the pairing.
The name the script used.
member.returns: The model's own name, or the name given when the room has nobody by it.
member.remarks: CHARACTERS.TXT is keyed by the three-letter model code, and the fallback of taking a name's first three letters only works where the two agree. They usually do — GABRIEL to GAB — and where they do not, nothing is found: Emilio's noun gives EMI and his section is [EML], so every question about him answered "there is no such character" and he stood where he was.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Modelled(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate,System.String)
member.summary: The same, for a caller that has the world rather than the scene.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Fidgeting(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate,System.Func{System.String,GK3Reborn.Formats.Animation.GasFile})
member.summary: Standing somebody at a named spot, without walking them there.

remarks.para: InitEgoPosition is how a room decides where the player is standing when they arrive. A scene's SCENE:ENTER action asks WasLastLocation which door they came through and stands them at the matching spot — the hallway alone has one for the lobby stairs and one for each of the guest rooms. Left recorded, every arrival is wherever the scene's [ACTORS] section put them, which is the front door however you got in.

It moves the camera as well, when the spot names one. That is the original's behaviour and it is the difference between arriving in a room and being teleported into it while the view stays where it was.

member.summary: Makes the fidget calls do something.
member.param: The host.
Where the characters are.
Where a named script is read from.

remarks.para: A fidget is what a character does when nobody is telling them to do anything, and GK3 gives every one of them three: idling, talking and listening. All seven calls were recorded, which is a cast standing perfectly still through every conversation in the game.

SetIdleGAS and its two relatives replace the script; StartIdleFidget and its relatives say which of the three to run whatever is happening; and StopFidget stands somebody still, which is what a script does before handing them something specific to do.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Showing(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate)
member.summary: Makes a scene's hidden staging appear and disappear.
member.param: The host.
The room the models stand in.
Where they are drawn.

remarks.para: GK3 stages a moment by leaving the pieces of it in the room, declared hidden, and having the script show them when they are wanted. ShowModel and HideModel were recorded and not performed, which meant every such moment happened with its subject missing.

RC1 at 102P is the case that was reported: on first leaving the hotel the scene shows wmo, plays the clip of it riding past, has Gabriel watch it and hides it again. With nothing shown, all the player got was Gabriel saying "A bike! Man, I need one of those" at an empty square — which reads as a line from some other part of the game playing by mistake.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Mood(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Puts an expression on somebody, or takes the one they are wearing off.
member.param: The host, for the mood the actor is currently wearing.
The room, for turning a noun into a model name.
What plays the animations.
Whose face, by either of their names.
The mood, or null to clear whatever is on.

remarks.para: The names are built from the model's three letters and the mood: gab plus angry plus on. Six moods are used across the game — confused, surprised, happy, angry, and half of the middle two — plus grief.
Setting one clears the last, because they are worn rather than stacked: the "off" animation is what puts the face back, and skipping it leaves an expression on somebody for the rest of the scene.

member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Aiming
member.summary: Where a walking call points, and which way to face when it gets there.
member.param: The spot on the floor to stand on.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Actor(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{GK3Reborn.Sheep.SheepValue},System.Int32)

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneScripting.Animating(GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate)
member.summary: Makes the animation calls move something.
member.param: The host.
What plays them.

remarks.para: The rigid part only. A clip's mesh transforms are applied and its vertex poses are not, which plays 2,188 of the corpus's 5,796 clips exactly right — a door, a drawer, a telephone — and plays a character as a set of mesh groups that move about without deforming. The second of those looks wrong and is still where the geometry goes.
They say how long they take through , so a waited animation holds up what follows it rather than being talked over.

member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.FidgetKind
member.summary: One of the three things a character does when nobody is telling them to do anything.
member.remarks: A scene's actor line names a script for each — idle=, talk=, listen= — and which of them is running is decided by who is speaking, unless a script has asked for one by name.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.FidgetKind.Idle
member.summary: Waiting: breathing, shifting weight, looking about.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.FidgetKind.Talk
member.summary: Speaking: the gestures that go with a line.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.FidgetKind.Listen
member.summary: Being spoken to.

member.name: T:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate
member.summary: What happens to a scene while nobody is doing anything to it.

remarks.para: Everything built so far happens because something asked: a click resolves an action, a script cuts the camera. This is the other half — the part of a game that runs on its own. A timer set a minute ago goes off; a head that was told to look at somebody arrives there rather than being there already.

It is deliberately the only thing that touches the clock. ADR 0004 forbids reading wall time anywhere but the platform layer, so the caller says how much time has passed and everything downstream is a function of that number: two runs stepped the same way do the same thing.

A head turns rather than snapping because that is the whole difference between a character glancing at you and a character who was always facing you. The rate is fixed rather than taken from the duration the scripts pass, because that argument's units are not established — lookitscenemodel("grace","cs2mntprthittest","h",100) is not a hundred seconds — and a plausible speed is better than a confident wrong one.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.GlideSeconds
member.summary: How long a glide takes, in seconds.
member.remarks: Fixed, like the turn rate and for the same reason: the scripts pass a duration whose units are not established. A second and a half is long enough to read as the camera moving rather than jumping, and short enough not to hold the player up.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.TurnRate
member.summary: How fast a head turns, in radians a second.
member.remarks: About 170 degrees a second: fast enough to read as noticing something, slow enough to read as a person doing it. A glance skips it.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.RunBeyond
member.summary: How much faster an actor moves when the player is in a hurry.

remarks.para: Gabriel's stride covers 49.9 units in 1.40 seconds — 35.6 units a second — and a walk plays at the stride's own pace so that his feet and the ground agree. That is what the game was authored at and it is genuinely slow to sit through when the player already knows where they are going.

So a double-click doubles it, and plays the stride at double speed to match. Not a separate run animation: only Gabriel has one in the archives — GABERUN, which belongs to a cutscene — and CHARACTERS.TXT names no run for anybody, so there is nothing to give the rest of the cast. A stride played faster reads as hurrying; a stride played at walking speed while the body slides along at twice it does not.

A setting rather than a constant: how impatient a double-click is belongs to the player, not to the game. One means a double-click does nothing but skip the walk's leisure, which is a legitimate answer for somebody who wants the pace the game was authored at.

member.summary: How far a walk has to be before it is run, in scene units.

remarks.para: A GK3 unit is roughly two and a half centimetres and a character stands about seventy tall, so this is a little over six metres — far enough that crossing it at a stroll is the player waiting rather than the player watching. Anything shorter is a step across a room and reads as fussy if it is taken at a trot.
It uses the same a double-click does, so a player who has turned that down to one has turned this off with it, which is the right thing for it to mean.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.WarpNextWalk
member.summary: Whether the next walk arrives at once instead of being walked.

remarks.para: Held with shift on a way out of the room. A player who knows where they are going has already watched that walk, and a second-floor corridor crossed for the ninth time is not the part of the game anybody came for.

One walk, and it clears itself. It is set immediately before an action is performed and consumed by the approach that action puts in front of itself, so a script's own walks are never affected — a cutscene that teleports its actor is a cutscene with a hole in it.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.DefaultHurryFactor
member.summary: The pace a double-click asks for unless the player has said otherwise.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate._logical
member.summary: Where each actor logically is, as against where their model is drawn.

remarks.para: The original keeps these apart and syncs one from the other every frame: GKActor::OnLateUpdate calls SyncActorToModelPositionAndRotation. So the model is the authority while something is driving it, and the actor's position is a follower that walking and scripts read.

That settles who owns an actor's position, which walking and animation both wanted to. Neither: the model does, and whichever of them is driving the model at the time gets it. Starting an animation stops a walk, so only one ever is.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate._held
member.summary: Models whose behaviour script is held while something else animates them.
member.remarks: A character has one animation at a time and a script asking for one outranks the idle they were running. The original pauses the idle rather than stopping it — GKProp::StartAnimation pauses and OnVertexAnimationStop resumes — so a character goes back to breathing where they left off once the scripted moment is over. Without it Gabriel's idle goes on choosing fidgets all the way through the coffee scene and every one of them fights the scene for his mesh groups.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.#ctor(GK3Reborn.Game.LoadedScene,GK3Reborn.Game.Gk3SheepApi,GK3Reborn.Game.Actors.Glances,GK3Reborn.Rendering.ISceneSink,GK3Reborn.Game.ActionResolver,GK3Reborn.Game.ActionRunner,GK3Reborn.Game.SheepScheduler)
member.summary: Creates an update for one standing scene.
member.param: The scene, already loaded.
The story host, for the timers it keeps.
Who is looking at what.
Where the scene was put, so heads can move in it.
What may be done to things, for timers coming due.
How to do it.
Scripts that are waiting for something, if anything is.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate._scenery
member.summary: Where the clips come from, when anything is to be played.
member.remarks: Optional. Without it finds nothing and animation calls go on being recorded, which is what every tool wants and what the launcher wanted until there was a reader.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate._chance
member.summary: What the cosmetic choices are drawn from.
member.remarks: Its own generator rather than the story's. GameState.NextRandom counts its draws into the state hash on purpose — two runs that have drawn a different number of times should disagree at once — and an idle picks a fidget every couple of seconds for as long as somebody stands in a room. Drawing those from the story would make the hash depend on how long the player loitered.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Animations
member.summary: Where the animations that name those clips come from.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Faces
member.summary: The faces in the room, when there is anything that can move one.
member.remarks: Optional, like the clips. Without it lip sync, blinking and expressions are all simply absent, and every character wears the bitmap they were modelled with — which is what a tool wants and what the launcher wanted before there was a compositor.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Animating
member.summary: How many clips are running.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Play(System.String,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Starts an animation.
member.param: What the script called it, such as GraCs3WrdbOpen.
Whether it starts again when it ends.

Whether the actor keeps the ground the clip covered. GK3 calls these move animations: an ordinary one leaves the pose where the clip finished but puts the actor's position and heading back where they were, so a character who mimes walking has not actually gone anywhere.

Whether a model's own behaviour script asked for it rather than the story. An idle gives way to the story and never the other way about: it is dropped where the story is already animating that model, and it is held while the story does.
member.returns: How long it will take, or zero when there is nothing to play.

remarks.para: A script names an .ANM, whose [ACTIONS] section names one or more .ACT clips and the frame each starts on. Each clip names the model it moves. None of those three names is the one the script said.

Only the rigid part plays: a clip's mesh transforms are applied, its vertex poses are not. That covers 2,188 of the corpus's 5,796 clips outright — doors, drawers, a telephone — and moves a character's mesh groups about without deforming any of them, which is wrong-looking but is where the geometry actually goes.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Sound
member.summary: What plays a sound an animation asks for, or null when there is no device.
member.remarks: A function rather than the audio object, so the world can be tested without one — the same shape as the clip and animation libraries. It is handed the cue and where in the room it comes from, and says whether anything was heard.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.StartScenery
member.summary: Starts every behaviour script the scene named.

remarks.para: Two kinds run. A gasprop carries one that lasts as long as the scene does — the lobby's ceiling fans turn because of one. An actor carries three: idle= for when nobody is telling them to do anything, talk= for while they are speaking and listen= for while somebody else is. Which of the three is running is decided every frame by who is talking.
Called once the scene is standing and its animation libraries are attached.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Open
member.summary: Puts everything the scene declared an opening pose for into it.
member.returns: How many were posed.

remarks.para: A SIF line may carry initanim=, and 316 of them across the corpus do. It is not something that happens — it says where the thing rests. RC1's copy of the hotel door is placed by Rc1PlaceLbyDoor; Madeline is stood by the van by MadRc1FigM; Emilio is sat in the lobby by EmlLbyBreathe. So the opening frame is sampled and the animation is not played, which is what Animator::Sample(anim, 0) does in the reference implementation.

The difference matters most for the ones that carry an absolute placement: playing them would take seven seconds to arrive at a pose that is meant to be true from the first frame, with the sounds and the footsteps of a door being opened by nobody.
Called once the clip and animation libraries are attached and before the room's SCENE:ENTER script runs, because that script asks where people are.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Posed
member.summary: Who an opening pose moved, where to, and which way they ended up facing.
member.remarks: Placed is the heading the model is standing at, out of the scene file. Wanted is the one the clip's opening frame implies, or null where the clip says nothing about it. Where the two disagree, the scene file is recording where the character ends up and the animation is stating where they begin.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.SetStride(System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Gives a character a different stride.
member.param: Their model name or noun.
The animation that gets them moving.
The stride itself, looped while they walk.
member.returns: True when the room has such a character.
member.remarks: SetWalkAnim, 42 calls: somebody walking differently for a while — carrying something, hurt, sneaking. It replaces what CHARACTERS.TXT said, so a walk begun after this uses the new one. The two turn animations the call also carries are read past: turning on the spot is done by the walker rather than by a clip.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate._strides
member.summary: What a character walks with now, when a script has changed it.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.StartScenery(System.String)
member.summary: Starts a prop's own script again.
member.param: Its model name or noun.
member.returns: True when the room has such a prop with a script.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.StopScenery(System.String)
member.summary: Stops a prop's own script.
member.param: Its model name or noun.
member.returns: True when one was running.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.SetBehaviour(System.String,GK3Reborn.Game.FidgetKind,GK3Reborn.Formats.Animation.GasFile)
member.summary: Gives a character a different script for one of the three things they do.
member.param: Their model name or noun.
Which of the three.
The script, or null to leave them with nothing to do.
member.returns: True when the room has such a character.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Quieten(GK3Reborn.Game.PlacedModel)
member.summary: Stops one model's behaviour script, because the story has taken it over.
member.param: The model.
member.remarks: GKActor::StartAnimation does this on the way in to any animation that did not come from the behaviour script itself. The prop the idle was holding goes back where it lives, which is what is for.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.StopFidget(System.String)
member.summary: Stops a character fidgeting, or everybody.
member.param: Their name, or null for everyone in the room.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Rest(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Playing)
member.summary: Puts a prop back where it lives, when the idle that was moving it is cut short.
member.param: The clip being stopped.

remarks.para: Reported as Emilio's newspaper and then as Mosely's: stop a character mid-idle and the paper stays in the air where his hands were. A GAS file may declare what to play if it is interrupted — USES CLEANUP, and 328 lines of the corpus are those — but mosPaperIdle.gas declares none, so there is nothing to play and no amount of looking for one will find it.

Only a prop, and only an idle. A character keeps whatever pose they were cut off in, which is right — a person stopped mid-gesture is a person standing oddly, not a person snapping to attention. And only an animation a behaviour started: an idle is decoration and may be interrupted at any moment, where a script's animation is the story and a door it left open is meant to stay open.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Tidy(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Fidget)
member.summary: Puts right whatever a behaviour script was in the middle of.
member.param: The character's scripts.
member.returns: True when there was something to put right.

remarks.para: A GAS file may declare a cleanup per animation — USES CLEANUP EmlLbyOpnPaper emllbyclspaper — meaning "if you stop me while I am doing the first, do the second". 328 of the corpus's 341 USE lines are these, and they exist because an idle can leave a character holding something: Emilio reads a newspaper in the lobby, and stopping him to shake Gabriel's hand without the cleanup leaves the paper hanging in the air where his hands used to be.
A cleanup may have a cleanup of its own, which is why this loops rather than playing one. Bounded, because a file that cleans up in a circle would otherwise not stop.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.StartFidget(System.String,GK3Reborn.Game.FidgetKind)
member.summary: Sets a character fidgeting again.
member.param: Their name.
Which of the three to run.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Speaking
member.summary: Told who is speaking, so that talking and listening can be told apart.
member.remarks: Set by the launcher from the faces, which know because the line being spoken names its own actor. Null leaves everybody idling, which is what a room with no audio should look like.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.StepBehaviours(System.Double)
member.summary: One step of every behaviour script that is running.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Conversation
member.summary: Which conversation is being held, or null between them.

member.name: F:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate._lent
member.summary: What each actor's own scripts were before a conversation replaced them.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.EnterConversation(System.String)
member.summary: Hands the actors in a conversation the scripts written for that conversation.
member.param: The conversation, as SetConversation names it.
member.returns: How long the actors take to get into it, in seconds.

remarks.para: A scene's [LISTENERS] section says what each participant does while speaking and while listening in this conversation, which is not what they do in general: Mosely leans on the counter of the Armorer's for two of its conversations and stands straight for the rest of the afternoon. 237 lines across 75 rooms say so.

The enter animation is what puts them into that pose, and its exit undoes it — so they are a pair and both have to run, or a character stays leaning on a counter for the rest of the day. What the actor had before is kept here rather than looked up again afterwards, because a second conversation may have replaced it in between.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.LeaveConversation
member.summary: Gives the actors their own scripts back, and undoes the poses.
member.returns: How long the actors take to come out of it, in seconds.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Restart(GK3Reborn.Game.PlacedModel)
member.summary: Starts an actor's fidget again, so a replaced script takes effect.
member.remarks: Swapping the file on the model changes what the next mode change runs, and a character already listening would go on running the script they were handed before the conversation began until somebody else spoke.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Tread(GK3Reborn.Formats.Animation.AnimationStep)
member.summary: Makes the noise a foot landing makes.
member.param: Whose foot, and whether it was dragged.

remarks.para: Three things have to agree and none of them is in the animation: which shoes the character is wearing (CHARACTERS.TXT), what the floor under them is made of (the texture, through FLOORMAP.TXT) and which of the three sounds for that pairing to use (FOOTSTEPS.TXT). The last is drawn from the room's own generator, so the same walk sounds the same twice.

Silent rather than wrong where any of the three is missing. A floor texture nothing classifies is most of the game's ceilings and walls, and a step on one should make no noise rather than a guessed one.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Names(GK3Reborn.Game.PlacedModel,System.String)
member.summary: Whether a name is one of a model's own.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Repaint(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{GK3Reborn.Formats.Animation.AnimationTexture})
member.summary: Applies an animation's texture swaps.
member.param: The changes due now.

remarks.para: The node names a mesh group and a submesh; the sink repaints by the texture the model was built with, because that is the thing it can find without knowing how a particular model is cut up. So the original is looked up from the model and used as the handle. A model the room does not have, or an index it does not go up to, is skipped in silence — animations are shared between rooms.

The replacement has to be resident before it can be drawn, and the scene loaded only what its models were painted with. So it is read and uploaded on first use and kept: Larry's alarm clock swaps through ten digits and would otherwise decode them again every second.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Textures
member.summary: Makes a texture resident, and says whether it could be.
member.remarks: A function rather than the archives, the same shape as the clip and animation libraries: without one nothing repaints, which is what a test with no device wants.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Crossing(GK3Reborn.Game.PlacedModel)
member.summary: Whether a model is walking somewhere, under either of its names.
member.remarks: A walk is filed under whichever name the caller used — a script says WalkTo("Gabriel", ...) and an action's approach says gab — so asking about one of the two answers "no" about half the walks in the game.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Same(GK3Reborn.Game.PlacedModel,System.String)
member.summary: Whether a name is one of a model's two.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Step(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Behaviour,System.Double)
member.summary: Runs one behaviour script forward by however much time has passed.
member.remarks: An animation is played and the script waits out its length before going on, which is what makes a fan turn continuously rather than restarting every frame. Sixteen instructions at once bounds a script that loops without ever waiting; the corpus has several, and without the bound one of them spins here for ever.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Notice(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Behaviour)
member.summary: Lets a behaviour notice somebody coming near, or leaving.
member.param: The script.

remarks.para: WHENNEAR Gabriel, 100, END is a standing condition, not an instruction: it holds for the whole of the script and jumps to its label on the frame its answer turns true, wherever execution happens to be — including the middle of a wait. This was parsed and never run, which is why Emilio sat on his bench for ever with Gabriel standing over him, and why the museum's whispering carried on however close Gabriel came: the interruption each script wrote for exactly that moment could never fire.

On the edge, exactly as the reference has it — GasPlayer::CheckDistanceConditions fires a condition when it goes from false to true and arms it again when it goes back. Level-triggered, a WHENNEAR would jump every frame for as long as anybody stood in the circle, and the label's own animation would restart sixty times a second.
Distance is flat, like every other nearness in the game: the spots carry heights the floor disagrees with, and a radius through the vertical answers "far away" about somebody standing on the mark.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Sees(System.String,System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: Whether one actor has another in front of them.
member.param: Whose sight, by either of their names.
Who they might see.
How wide their sight is, in degrees, as the script states it.
member.returns: True when the second is inside the first's field of view.

remarks.para: WHENINVIEW Gabriel, 90, INSULT: Mosely insults Gabriel when Gabriel comes into his view. The number is an angle rather than a distance — the two conditions that are about distance carry one, and these carry 90 and 70, which are fields of view and not room-sized radii.

Read as the whole field rather than a half-angle, so 90 means 45 degrees either side of the way the actor is facing. Both readings are defensible from the data and neither corpus use is load-bearing — Mosely's insult and Gabriel's yawn — so this takes the reading that matches what a field of view usually means.
Flat, like every other sight line here: a character looking across a room is not looking up or down, and heights the floor disagrees with would answer "behind me" about somebody standing on a step.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Say(System.String)
member.summary: Says one line, and answers how long it lasts.
member.param: The licence plate the line is filed under.
member.returns: Seconds the line takes, or zero when nothing can play it.
member.remarks: Through the same API a script uses, rather than through the animation library directly: a line is a run of animations, a caption and a voice, and which of those happen is the dialogue layer's business and not a behaviour script's.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Restore(GK3Reborn.Game.PlacedModel)
member.summary: Puts an actor back where the scene placed them.
member.param: The model to move.
member.remarks: The authored transform, which the record still carries: moving a model writes the geometry rather than the placement, so what the scene said is never lost and this restores the facing as well as the spot. Whatever they were doing stops, because they are not where they were doing it any more.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Flat(System.Numerics.Vector3)
member.summary: A distance squared, measured across the ground plan.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Choose(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Behaviour)
member.summary: Takes one of the choices in the run starting where the script is.
member.remarks: Weighted, and the weights do not have to add to anything: the corpus writes 100, 100, 50, 50 and means a half chance each of the first two. The whole run is stepped over afterwards, however long it is, because it was one decision.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Rescript(GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Behaviour,System.String)
member.summary: Puts a different script in a running behaviour's place.

member.name: P:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Behaviours
member.summary: Where a behaviour script named by another one is read from.
member.remarks: Only NEWIDLE needs it, and only a caller with the archives can answer. Null leaves the character running what they were running, which is what a tool wants.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Send(System.String,System.String)

member.summary: Finds a model the room places, by either of its names.

member.remarks: Both halves matter: the geometry stops drawing it, and the model itself remembers, so that the picker does not go on offering a noun for something nobody can see.

member.summary: Applies an animation's visibility changes.

remarks.para: A model the room does not have is skipped in silence. Animations are shared between rooms and an [MVISIBILITY] line naming something that is not here is as ordinary as an [ACTIONS] line doing the same.

The per-part form — <frame>,<model>,<mesh>,<submesh>,on — is not distinguished from the whole-model form here: the sink draws a placement, not a submesh of one, and hiding the whole thing is the closer of the two answers. Only a handful of the corpus's lines use it.

Whether it is drawn.
member.returns: True when the room has an object by that name.
member.remarks: The room rather than a model standing in it: see . The picker is told as well, because a doorway a script has just closed off must stop answering to clicks — otherwise the noun goes on being offered for something nobody can see.

member.summary: Whether a script is animating somebody right now.
member.param: Their model name or noun.
member.returns: True while a clip the story asked for is playing on them.

remarks.para: A story's animation and a character's own idle are not the same thing and must not be interrupted the same way. An idle is decoration and a click may cut it short at any moment; a clip a script started is the scene happening, and walking out of the middle of it leaves the story mid-sentence with nobody in the room it is addressed to.
Reported from the dining room: a click on the floor during the coffee scene sent Gabriel away while the scene went on around where he had been standing.

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.Release(System.String)

member.name: M:GK3Reborn.Game.SceneUpdate.BehaviourOf(System.String)
member.summary: The script a model runs on its own, whichever kind of thing it is.
member.remarks: A prop carries one script for as long as the scene stands; a character carries three and runs whichever suits who is talking. Both end up as the same thing here.

member.summary: Who the game's characters are, and how each of them walks.
member.remarks: Null leaves everybody sliding: an actor with no stride still crosses the room, in whatever pose they were standing in. That is what a partial set has to do — the walk is read from CHARACTERS.TXT, and not every model in the game is in it.

member.remarks: Optional, like the clips: without it nobody makes a noise walking, which is what the game did before this and what a test with no audio wants.
